reference_solution: January first print was 353; March 8 revised January to 229 and first published February at 275. March 8 revised December 333→290 and January 353→229, giving (290−333)+(229−353)=−43−124=−167. April 5 revised January 229→256 and February 275→270, giving +27−5=+22; its March first print was 303. The mixed first-print sum is 353+275+303=931. The single April 5 vintage Q1 sum is 256+270+303=829. Their difference is 829−931=−102, also (256−353)+(270−275)=−97−5=−102. Adding the two release-wide revision totals would incorrectly give −145 because it includes a −43 December revision outside Q1. The desk's tracked cumulative amount increases from 229+275=504 to 829, a change of 325=303+22. This last quantity combines new March coverage and revisions; it is not a surprise against a forecast. April 5's official 08:30 ET release time corresponds to 12:30 UTC because daylight saving time was in effect; the task cutoff conservatively uses end of that UTC day.

limitations: This prototype tests explicit historical vintage reconstruction and numerical/citation checks. It does not establish novelty relative to all existing benchmarks or measure investment performance.
All three source excerpts are shown together. Earlier-vintage outputs are reconstructed retrospectively; no actual committed answer or staged tool release is enforced.
Historical source cutoffs do not remove information encoded in model training; do not interpret results as leakage-free historical forecasting.

Raw HTML could not be captured because direct BLS access returned HTTP 403. Frozen evidence consists of the exact actual web-tool responses and supported narrative/table excerpts, not a byte-identical full original release. Independent recapture remains pending.
The official archive header supplies an announced release time rather than independently verified first access; the task uses an end-of-day cutoff.

Numeric sums are sums of reported monthly changes in the requested vintages. No unrevised true employment count, benchmark-final value, statistical significance, market consensus surprise, or P&L is inferred.

Citation fact groups accept separate verbatim input clauses and summary-table alternatives, not all possible derivations or causal claims. Legitimate evidence outside the declared source/group alternatives requires manual review and is not automatically accepted.
